## Phase 6 — `@AfterReturning` aspects (enrich the response `OwnerDto` only — no storage effect)

23. **`OwnerMembershipNumberAdvice`** — sets `membershipNumber = <customerCode>-M<YY>`.
24. **`OwnerCheckDigitAdvice`** — sets `checkDigit` (Luhn over `customerCode`).
25. **`OwnerBulkSignupWarningAdvice`** — sets `bulkSignupWarning = (createdToday > 80)`.
26. **`OwnerNamesakeCountAdvice`** — sets `namesakeCount` (lower-id owners sharing first+last name) and invokes `MembershipPoints.assign`.
27. **`MembershipPoints`** — sets `membershipPoints` and `membershipLevel`.

Plus MapStruct `@AfterMapping` hooks on `toOwnerDto` populate derived read-only fields: `householdId`, `identityKey`, `locality`, `contactPreference`, `ageBand`, `telephoneDisplay`.

## Finally

28. `Location: /api/owners/{id}` header set; response returned as **201 Created**.

**Error mapping:** the 409/429 `ResponseStatusException`s from the aspects are mapped by `ResponseStatusExceptionAdvice` (highest precedence); validation failures → 400; `DataIntegrityViolation` → 404; catch-all → 500.

One thing worth flagging: several of these are non-standard for a Spring app — validation logic and payload mutation are spread across `@InitBinder` validators and AspectJ advices rather than living in the DTO/service, so the effective behavior (address/phone normalization, capacity/rate/duplicate gates, response enrichment) isn't visible from the controller or entity alone.
